page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v6 is a memory-intensive server instance belonging to the Famsv6 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with one thread per core. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ams_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores both rank in the top 10% tier. Software compilation using Clang and image processing tasks also achieve top-tier performance. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is robust, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 7120.47 GB/sec and large block uncached read bandwidth at 226.16 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Large-model LLM inference (70B) and single-threaded compression tasks represent moderate performance tiers, scoring in the middle 50%.

The server does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning workloads requiring local scratch space or GPU acceleration must rely on external premium storage or alternative instance types. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F48ams_v6 offers high memory density relative to its dedicated physical core count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local disk storage. The instance is suited for database operations, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
